## bab4d8f5ba7a

**Classification: Suspected shortcut / curriculum packing risk.** The assigned generator SHA-256 is `6b48b50cfbabd0a320318c122f6c77f8b90e8de052e20cfa2e622eab6bdeae02`, matching the audit contract. Its declared rule hash `1130750019d1` also matches the live executed/catalog hash.

The generator’s five teaching profiles are selected only by `(sample_index + difficulty_shift) % 5`. I reproduced a stride-aliasing failure over **300 ordinary default inputs**: three bands × five residues × 20 examples. Every stride-5 residue contained exactly one teaching profile, and every one-profile shard left at least one of the generator’s own declared canonical shortcuts answer-equivalent on all 20/20 examples. By contrast, all 15 contiguous five-example control windows (three bands × five cyclic starts) contained all five profiles and left no declared shortcut alive.

All 300 sampled inputs passed the target validator and belong to its documented default domain. Live Racket was applied to 15 representative inputs (one per band/residue) and matched the generator mirror **15/15**, so this is not an oracle-correctness complaint; it is a lesson assembly risk. Evidence and the reusable reproducer are in `checks/audit/bab4d8f5ba7a/schedule_alias_report.json`, `audit_schedule.py`, and `racket.json`.

A practical fix would randomize the curriculum phase with a source-bound shard/lesson identifier or make the packer explicitly mix residues, then run a window-level rival-survival gate on the actual packed order. The target was audit-only and remains unchanged.

## bab4d8f5ba7a

**Classification: reproduced shortcut-compatible sharding risk, not a defect in
the standard consecutive lesson path.** The assigned generator hash is
`6b48b50cfbabd0a320318c122f6c77f8b90e8de052e20cfa2e622eab6bdeae02`.
The teaching schedule has period five. A four-demo stride-5 lesson using seed
211, easy difficulty, and sample indices `[0, 5, 10, 15]` yields four valid
`canonical_single` scenes. Against actual Racket outputs, all three declared
public-corpus shortcuts survive the entire lesson:
`first_marker_only`, `zero_header_recolors`, and `erase_nonmarker_body`.

`checks/audit-bab4d8f5ba7a-stride5.json` contains every input, authoritative
output, rival output, observed profile, validation result, hashes, and the exact
reproducer. This is scoped: the repository’s normal consecutive lesson
assembly is not affected. The target’s focused tests pass 9/9
(`checks/audit-bab4d8f5ba7a-tests.log`) and its standard semantic gate passes
(`checks/audit-bab4d8f5ba7a-semantic-console.log`). The risk appears only if a
downstream sharder/interleaver uses a stride congruent to the schedule period. I
did not modify this audit target.

triage.reason: Both audit reports retained against exact target hashes; census results remain reviewer-reported. Repair targets are not modified by audits. Findings are visible to future assignments via task indexes.
